pr.title: Brighten selected item colors and keep hints in the footer
pr.head: 9058f9b7c00606786399cb62e9b5c3c895f8e791

summary: The console lists sessions and the inbox items that need attention. Focus now brightens each item’s existing color, so a selected question stays blue and a selected request stays orange. Session names and plain labels use bright gray, with bold text to make focus visible without color.

The agent console keeps shortcuts on its bottom hint line. The session list offers new-session and navigation actions; chat and launch editors show their own actions. Removing the hint from the list also removes an extra body row.

cards.title: Review result
cards.html: Clean at 9058f9b. All five changed files were reviewed; no findings, suggestions, or follow-ups remain.

cards.title: Validation
cards.html:
• The configured review gate passed, including both plugin validations, 270 hook tests, hook type checking, and diff whitespace checks.
  • tests.test_console and tests.test_agent_console passed all 113 tests, including native terminal mouse checks.
  • Additional palette checks covered dark and light themes with 8, 16, and 256 colors. No physical terminal or live provider session was exercised.

groups.title: Keep item colors when focus moves
groups.kicker: Build focused styles once, then apply them to the selected text.
intro: The shared renderer used to paint every focused label with the suggestion color. The palette now supplies a focused variant of each semantic style. Color-capable terminals brighten the existing color; bold supplies a second focus cue.

checks.text: Traced session names, inbox subjects, options, and action labels through the shared renderer. Focus applies to the label text, while neighboring spans and drag selection keep their behavior.
Confirmed palette setup happens when the screen is created rather than on each draw. The change adds no network, file, or provider calls.

files.note: Read the palette construction before the renderer: named styles get focus variants, while plain labels use the dedicated gray focus style.

checks.text: Exercised 8-, 16-, and 256-color palettes under dark and light theme settings; every foreground stays within the terminal’s advertised color range.
Checked the focused-style fallback and existing selection handling. Rich-color tests confirm selected inbox labels preserve their orange, blue, or gray family.

files.note: The tests check selected session names are gray and selected inbox labels brighten without losing their kind color. Native mouse coordinates move up with the removed body hint.

checks.text: The focused test run passed the new dark- and light-theme assertions along with the existing monochrome, basic-color, clipping, drag-selection, and native mouse coverage.

groups.title: Put shortcuts at the bottom
groups.kicker: Keep each view’s actions on one footer line.
intro: The agent console’s home view now returns its hints from the existing footer method. An empty list omits selection and open actions, and a home-view status message occupies that same line. The old body-list hint is removed.

checks.text: Followed home, chat, launch-prompt, and settings transitions. Each view reaches its own footer, and the home hint does not appear inside the other views.

files.note: The home footer handles both status messages and available shortcuts; removing the home_lines override avoids reserving an extra list row.

checks.text: Checked the empty and populated list branches, footer width fitting, and the existing field-specific footer paths.

files.note: One flow checks the bottom row, available actions on an empty or populated session list, and hint changes when opening chat or launch settings.

checks.text: The new flow passed within the 113-test focused run. Its fake screen asserts that the new-session hint appears only on the final row.

files.note: The CLI guide describes gray session focus, brighter semantic inbox colors, and shortcuts for the current view.

checks.text: Compared the documented hints and focus colors with the updated footer and palette branches.
